title: Cameroon: ghost workers in the AI machine
content: African states want to develop AI attuned to local needs and cultures. But for educated young Africans, the reality of the AI revolution looks more like poorly paid, precarious work for Western firms.

title: A chill in Uzbekistan's cultural spring
content: Since the death of its iron dictator a decade ago, Uzbekistan is keen to rewrite its image through the arts. But beneath talk of intellectual openness, propaganda is still rife and new taboos are emerging.

title: Nature gains legal rights in Spain
content: A lagoon on Spain's Mediterranean coast is the first ecosystem in Europe to gain legal personhood, and now it's taking its polluters to court. But it's up against bureaucracy and local economic interests.

title: Neighbours, but still not friends

title: Who wants peace?
content: Who in the Arab world really wants peace? While war rages on in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, and within Libya, Sudan and Yemen, no major initiative is emerging to stop the fighting or prevent new conflicts breaking out, such as those brewing between Egypt and Ethiopia over the Nile waters, and between Algeria and Morocco, where tensions have continued to rise since the two countries severed diplomatic relations in August 2021. The Arab Maghreb Union (AMU) is all but dead, and the Arab League is (…)

title: Saudi Arabia: no good option over Yemen
content: Unprecedented Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have exposed its vulnerability. And with Donald Trump reluctant to intervene and other potential allies holding back, Iran's position is only strengthened.

title: Down among the deep-sea drones
content: Navies around the world are racing to deploy deep-sea drones known as autonomous underwater vehicles. These machines promise to transform the exploration – and control – of the ocean depths.
